title: runners.toml v2 must fail readably on an older tk, not with 57 unknown-key errors
description:
BLOCKER found live (2026-08-19), immediately after sqt migrated this repo. Reproduced by experiment, not inference:
  installed tk 0.30.0  -> tk herd spawn FAILS: ".tick/runners.toml: 57 validation errors: environment.commands: unknown key (a typo is an error, never silently ignored); ..."
  tk built from this branch -> spawn succeeds

We designed the compatibility we expected (new tk reads legacy markdown) and missed its mirror image: OLD TK READS NEW TOML. Because 728 correctly made unknown keys fail closed, an older tk does not degrade — it dies on every herd command with a wall of unknown-key errors that names no cause and no fix. Any operator or teammate on a released tk is hard-broken the moment someone runs tk config migrate, and the error gives them nothing to act on.

runners.toml already carries a version field, which exists for exactly this. Fix:
1. Bump the schema/file version when the new tables are present (version = 2).
2. Make the loader check version FIRST and, when the file is newer than the binary understands, fail with one actionable line — .tick/runners.toml is version 2 and this tk understands version 1; upgrade tk (tk upgrade) — instead of enumerating unknown keys.
3. tk config migrate must write the new version, and should warn that the migrated file needs a tk of at least the version that introduced it.
4. Keep unknown-key-fails-closed for keys WITHIN a version the binary does understand — that behaviour is right and 728 should not be weakened. This is about the version gate coming first.

Note the orchestrator is now driving this run with a branch-built tk; the installed 0.30.0 cannot operate this repo at all until it is upgraded.

acceptance_criteria: A runners.toml carrying the new tables reports version 2; a tk that understands only version 1 fails with a single actionable upgrade message naming the versions, not a list of unknown keys; a typo inside a supported version still fails closed naming the key; tk config migrate writes the new version and says which tk version is required.
